### Summary

Codex computer-use install could omit owner authorization. In affected versions, an authorized non-owner channel sender could install a Codex plugin and cause its configured MCP process to start on the OpenClaw host.

This advisory is scoped to the Codex computer-use installation command. Installed plugins remain trusted code under OpenClaw's security model; the failed boundary is authorization to install that code in the first place.

### Impact

A non-owner sender with command access could install attacker-selected plugin code and execute a host MCP process with the OpenClaw user's privileges. This could affect host confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable Codex computer-use installation in message channels and review installed Codex plugins for unexpected entries.
summary: Codex computer-use install could omit owner authorization
